title.narrative: Output 1.4. Increased capacity of Member States to improve social dialogue and labour relations laws, processes and institutions

description.narrative:
Manual on risk mapping of industrial relations situation issued in April 2022 by the Ministry of Manpower to strengthen the capacity of mediators for dispute prevention; Through this exercise, mediators are required to identify industrial relations risks in each respective area. In addition to that, mediators’ capacities and skills are improved for addressing disputes especially those created during the Covid-19 pandemic. Strengthened dispute resolution mechanism at the workplace level for garment companies registered with the BWI program. 2022 has been marked by cases involving alleged trade union discrimination. The programme supported employers and unions in at least 21 industrial disputes in Better Work Indonesia factories, most of them concerning alleged anti-union behaviour. Along with ILO inputs supported by RBSA intervention for Outcome 1.4 to improve the curricula for mediation and socialization of risk mapping manual to all mediators, ILO also facilitated capacity building of the mediators through US Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service (FMCS). With this support, the operational procedure of case handling by mediators is improved.
The role of BWI during the dispute resolution process includes encouraging social dialogue and the resolution of the dispute at the bipartite level and appealing to the national dispute settlement mechanism if required. BWI also maintains communication with the union at the branch/national levels, and brands and consults with the Ministry of Manpower whenever an escalation is needed to support the resolution process. Also, in situations where the role of the local Manpower office needs to be strengthened, BWI often reaches out to the Ministry of Manpower (national level) to support dispute resolution. BWI promotes the use of the national dispute system during industrial relations disputes that happened in 2022, four conflicts were resolved at the bipartite level, seven disputes were decided through mediation and three of them went up to the industrial court. The rest of the 7 cases are still undergoing the bipartite and/or mediation process.

description.narrative: Sectoral social dialogue forum called JAGA SAWITAN (Employment Network for Sustainable Palm Oil) was established between the Indonesian Palm Oil Workers' Union Network (JAPBUSI) and the Indonesia Palm Oil Employers' Association (GAPKI) to improve working conditions and promote collective bargaining in this sector. The ILO has supported capacity building for improving social dialogue and industrial relations in the palm oil sector since 2014. Advancing Workers’ Rights in Indonesia and Malaysia’s Palm Oil Sector (IDN/18/02/USA) assisted in developing educational programs for workers' and employers' organizations, to ensure active participation in social dialogue and expand their outreach, organization, and collective action.
